items.title: How a metabolite protects the enzyme that consumes it
items.summary: Metabolites are consumed by enzymes to produce other vital molecules as well as to control metabolite levels. But how do cells avoid consuming too much? Researchers from the MPI of Biochemistry, with the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, and the de Duve Institute in Brussels, have deciphered such molecular regulation in tryptophan metabolism. The essential amino acid tryptophan binds to a second site on the enzyme TDO2, distinct from where it is consumed. This sequesters a region needed by two effectors, the kinase CK2 and the ubiquitin ligase CUL1–β-TrCP, which act sequentially to signal TDO2 degradation. The findings are now published in Molecular Cell.

items.title: SynFit guides enzyme engineering by balancing several useful traits at once
items.summary: Enzymes are biology's tiny chemists. They help build, break and rearrange molecules quickly and precisely. In the lab, scientists have long put enzymes to work making useful chemicals. But nature's enzymes cannot do every reaction a researcher might want. Sometimes scientists need an enzyme to take on a job it did not evolve to do. That's where enzyme engineering comes in—researchers make changes to an enzyme, test how those changes affect what the enzyme does and look for versions that work better.

England forward Owen Trout served a one-month ban after testing positive for cannabis. Wong, 30, is among hundreds of Hongkongers detained under the controversial national security law. Concacaf's new Gold Cup format will feature two groups of eight teams, with the change designed to create more meaningful matchups during the group stage. Previously played with four groups of four, the 2027 edition of the competition will have two groups of eight with teams sorted into "ranking bands." Teams will play four group matches instead of the previous three, with the top four teams in each group moving into the quarterfinals. The bands will separate teams into levels based on their Concacaf ranking. Teams will meet an opponent from each band, meaning the strongest team in a group will play a team from Band 2, Band 3 and Band 4.

A British man being treated for Ebola in Congo is being evacuated to the UK, the government said Thursday. LONDON — A British man being treated for Ebola in Congo is being evacuated to the UK, the government said Thursday. The patient is expected to be taken to the Royal Free Hospital in London, which has a high-level isolation unit that was used to treat patients from an Ebola outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015.

The ocean’s blue and green hues near the infamous zone of debris have gotten brighter over the last 20 years, satellite data show The Great Pacific Garbage Patch , an area in the Pacific Ocean where debris naturally accumulates, is full of tiny bits of plastic. So full, in fact, that it seems to be changing the color of the ocean. The ocean is, of course, famously blue. That’s due to the wavelength of light it reflects . Water scatters shorter wavelengths, which we see as blue—while absorbing longer wavelengths such as red or orange. Additives in the ocean can affect its color, including phytoplankton, algae and sediment.

Using a capture card and open-source software to run PS5 video through a PC GPU. On an explicitly unmoderated GTAVI subreddit, user RevolutionaryBus8208 lays out a proposed setup, which runs a PS5 through a 4K capture card to a PC. From there, the video signal is run through Veyra , an open source tool that can apply DLSS 5’s AI-powered “neural rendering” to video content. The result—which also uses DLSS frame generation to increase the 30 fps source to a 90 fps output—is then piped back to a 4K TV, theoretically adding some of the benefits of a beefy PC graphics card to a console-exclusive game.

California has historically had the largest population of death row inmates in the US. California Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the death sentences of all 548 people on death row in the state, changing them instead with life in prison. "We can now let these offenders die in obscurity while we forever remember and honour the victims," he said in a letter. The decision to spare death row inmates is largely symbolic in a state that has not executed a prisoner since 2006, though experts say it could save millions of dollars in court costs each year. Only 13 inmates have been killed since voters reinstated the death penalty in 1978.

Law bans social media platforms from providing minors features such as autoplay that lead to compulsive use Google, Meta and TikTok sued California to block enforcement of ⁠a new state law intended ⁠to limit the risk ​of addicting children under 16 to social media platforms. The law, known as Assembly Bill 1709, prohibits such platforms from offering underage children “psychologically exploitative features” that could lead to compulsive use, such as providing ⁠personal recommendations and sending videos through autoplay features. An unprecedented early weakening of the polar vortex is causing uncertainty amongst experts over the impact it will have on UK weather as Simon King explains. High above the Arctic, powerful winds usually circle the North Pole each winter, helping trap some of the coldest air on Earth. But this circulation, known as the polar vortex, has weakened and shifted position in recent days. While such disruptions can occur during winter, scientists say an event this early in November is unprecedented in modern observations.

A Kenyan court has sentenced the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children. Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.

Explaining the Great Unconformity, where Cambrian deposits sit on top of older rocks. In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth’s mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet’s interior.

Only 17 of the top 100 players in the 2027 draft class are set to have their eligibility expire Five-for-five plays out exactly how you think. College players have five years of service available to them before they've exhausted their NCAA eligibility, no matter whether they took a redshirt year or not. What this means is that true seniors, players who got on the field for four years without burning a redshirt, are no longer getting pushed out of the NCAA, but actually have another year of eligibility. I first got wind of this upcoming trend in October, so I decided to look at the upcoming class and how it would impact it. My finding: It could impact it a lot.

(AP) — Logan O’Connor thinks of his late father in pregame warmup. He thinks of him sometimes in the middle of a game, too. His father, former NHL defenseman Myles O'Connor, died suddenly last month. He was 59 years old. "The reason I play is because he was my hero," O'Connor said Friday after an optional practice. "I wanted to be just like him." His father was a captain for the University of Michigan hockey squad before being drafted in the third round by the New Jersey Devils in 1985. Myles O'Connor played a total of 43 games over his career with three goals. He also had four assists — five, if assisting in getting his son to fall in love with the game and become an NHL player counts.

It's the exact path, not the apparent severity that matters most, doctors say. Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a “moderate” brain injury, just one point above “mild.” He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5).

Men's college soccer won't be a two-semester sport after all following a vote of Division I schools. Two-thirds of Division I schools rescinded a previously approved rule change to college soccer's calendar, the NCAA announced Friday, Nov. 6. The rule change would've moved the men's college soccer national championship to the spring semester; now, it will remain during the fall. The sport's oversight committee had previously adopted the rule change in May. Men's college soccer moving to a two-semester sport was also recommended by U.S. Soccer, the highest governing body in the country.

The Leonid meteor shower, known for its bright and fast meteors, will kick off this weekend and continue until the end of November. The Leonid meteor shower is set to dazzle sky gazers across the UK throughout November. The celestial spectacle takes place from now until 30 November with the peak taking place on the night of 17 November. The shower is made up of dust particles from the Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which leaves a trail of debris as it follows its path around the Sun. These particles enter the Earth's atmosphere at up to 44 miles (71km) per second - meaning these streaks of light are the fastest meteors in the sky.
